class PostAdmin(ModelView):
    column_display_pk = True
    column_list = [
        "id",
        "user",
        "user.email",
        "title",
        "date",
        "tags",
        "background_color",
        "created_at",
    ]
    column_editable_list = [
        "background_color",
    ]
    column_default_sort = ("date", True)
    create_modal = True
    edit_modal = True
    column_sortable_list = [
        "id",
        "title",
        "date",
        "user.email",
        ("user", ("user.last_name", "user.first_name")),  # sort on multiple columns
    ]
    column_searchable_list = [
        "title",
        "tags.name",
        "user.first_name",
        "user.last_name",
    ]
    column_labels = {
        "title": "Post Title",
        "tags.name": "Tags",
        "user.first_name": "User's first name",
        "user.last_name": "Last name",
    }
    column_filters = [
        "id",
        "user.first_name",
        "user.id",
        "background_color",
        "created_at",
        "title",
        "date",
        "tags",
        filters.FilterLike(
            Post.title,
            "Fixed Title",
            options=(("test1", "Test 1"), ("test2", "Test 2")),
        ),
        # Filter instances also accept a dotted-path string for ``column``;
        # it is resolved against the view's model and the necessary joins
        # are added automatically. Paths can traverse multiple
        # relationships, e.g. Post -> user -> account -> username.
        filters.FilterLike(column="user.email", name="Author Email"),
        filters.FilterInList(
            column="user.account.provider",
            name="Author's Account Provider",
            options=[(e.value, e.value) for e in AccountProvider],
        ),
    ]
    can_export = True
    export_max_rows = 1000
    export_types = ["csv", "xls"]

    # Pass arguments to WTForms. In this case, change label for text field to
    # be 'Big Text' and add DataRequired() validator.
    form_args = {"text": dict(label="Big Text", validators=[validators.DataRequired()])}
    form_widget_args = {"text": {"rows": 10}}

    form_ajax_refs = {
        "user": {"fields": (User.first_name, User.last_name)},
        "tags": {
            "fields": (Tag.name,),
            "minimum_input_length": 0,  # show suggestions, even before any user input
            "placeholder": "Please select",
            "page_size": 5,
        },
    }

    def __init__(self, session):
        # Just call parent class with predefined model.
        super().__init__(Post, session)

I couldn't fix this yet, because I haven't reproduced your 500 in your own app. The only 500 I've reproduced has a different cause that probably doesn't apply to you.

This directory is the flask-admin library itself, not your app. I found no admin page of yours with a required tags field, so I tested two setups:

- **Bundled `examples/sqla` app with `DataRequired()` on `tags`:** saving with no tags returns a normal 200 with the "This field is required" message.
- **Minimal app of my own with the same validator:** this gave the 500. The traceback ends in `KeyError: 'babel'`, raised from `flask_admin/babel.py:58` when the required message is translated. That app had `flask_babel` installed but never called `Babel(app)`. The example app does call it, which is why it works.

If your app has `flask_babel` installed but doesn't initialise it, the fix is to add `Babel(app)`. Otherwise, uninstall `flask_babel` and flask-admin falls back to untranslated messages. Alternatively, I could make `Translations` in `babel.py` fall back to the plain string when Babel isn't set up. I haven't made that change because it's a library change for a cause I haven't confirmed in your app.

Can you paste the traceback from your server log for the 500, or tell me where your app's code lives? If it ends in `KeyError: 'babel'`, I'll apply whichever fix you prefer. If it's something else, I'll chase that instead.
